title: Sum of digits
statement: Given a non-negative whole number, add up its digits. For 4096 the answer is 4 + 0 + 9 + 6 = 19.
input: The first line has T, the number of test cases. Each of the next T lines has one number n.
output: For each test case, print the sum of the digits of n on its own line.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 10^18 (use long long in C++ and long in Java)
hint: n % 10 gives the last digit and n / 10 removes it.

title: Reverse a number
statement: Write the digits of a number in reverse order. Leading zeros disappear, so 1200 becomes 21.
input: The first line has T. Each of the next T lines has one number n.
output: For each test case, print n with its digits reversed.

constraints: Checking divisors up to √n is fast enough; checking up to n is not.
hint: Only test divisors i while i * i <= n. Use long long for i * i.

title: GCD and LCM
statement: Find the greatest common divisor and the least common multiple of two numbers. For 12 and 18 they are 6 and 36.
input: The first line has T. Each of the next T lines has two numbers a and b.
output: For each test case, print the GCD and the LCM separated by a space.
constraints: 1 ≤ a, b ≤ 10^9 (the LCM can reach 10^18, so use long long / long)

title: Count the vowels

hint: Read whole lines: getline in C++, readLine in Java. After reading T with cin, call getline once to skip the rest of that line.

title: Smallest and largest
statement: Find the smallest and the largest value in an array.
input: The first line has T. Each test case has a line with n, then a line with n numbers.
output: For each test case, print the smallest and the largest value separated by a space.
hint: Start both answers at a[0], not at 0: every value might be negative.

title: Second largest
statement: Find the second largest distinct value in an array. Repeated values count once, so in 5 5 3 the answer is 3. If there is no second distinct value, print -1.
input: The first line has T. Each test case has a line with n, then a line with n numbers.
output: For each test case, print the second largest distinct value, or -1.
constraints: Try to do it in one pass without sorting.

title: Rectangle class
statement: Write a Rectangle class that stores a width and a height, with methods area() and perimeter(). Use it to answer each test case.
input: The first line has T. Each of the next T lines has a width w and a height h.
output: For each test case, print the area and the perimeter separated by a space.
constraints: 1 ≤ w, h ≤ 10^9 (the area needs long long / long)

title: Adding fractions
statement: Write a Fraction class with a numerator and a denominator that always keeps itself in lowest terms with a positive denominator. Overload + (in C++) or write add() (in Java), and add two fractions.
input: The first line has T. Each of the next T lines has two fractions written as a/b c/d.
output: For each test case, print the sum as p/q in lowest terms, with q > 0. Zero is written 0/1.

output: For each test case, print the total area with exactly one digit after the decimal point.

title: Pair with target sum
statement: Given an array and a target, find the two positions i < j whose values add up to the target. Exactly one such pair exists. Positions start at 0.
input: The first line has T. Each test case has a line with n and target, then a line with n numbers.
output: For each test case, print i and j separated by a space.
constraints: An O(n) solution with a hash map is expected; O(n²) also passes these limits.
hint: Walk left to right, remembering each value's position in a map. For each new value x, check whether target - x is already in the map.

title: Binary search
statement: Given a sorted array of distinct numbers, find the position of x, or print -1 if it is not there. Positions start at 0. Use binary search, not a loop over every element.
input: The first line has T. Each test case has a line with n and x, then a line with the n sorted numbers.
output: For each test case, print the position of x or -1.

title: Maximum subarray sum
statement: Find the largest sum of a contiguous, non-empty part of an array. In -2 1 -3 4 -1 2 1 -5 4 the best part is 4 -1 2 1, with sum 6.
input: The first line has T. Each test case has a line with n, then a line with n numbers.
output: For each test case, print the largest sum.
constraints: -10^4 ≤ each value ≤ 10^4 (sums need long long / long)
hint: Keep the best sum of a part that ends at the current element: either the element alone, or the element added to the previous best.

title: Longest part without repeats
statement: Find the length of the longest contiguous part of a string in which no letter repeats. In abcabcbb it is abc, length 3.
input: The first line has T. Each of the next T lines is a lowercase string.
output: For each string, print the length.

title: K-th largest
statement: Find the k-th largest value in an array. Equal values count separately, so in 3 3 1 the 2nd largest is 3. A min-heap of size k, or sorting, both work.
input: The first line has T. Each test case has a line with n and k, then a line with n numbers.
output: For each test case, print the k-th largest value.

title: Count the islands
statement: A map is a grid of 1s (land) and 0s (water). An island is a group of land cells joined up, down, left or right (not diagonally). Count the islands. Use BFS or DFS.
input: The first line has T. Each test case has a line with r and c, then r lines of c characters, each 0 or 1.
output: For each test case, print the number of islands.
hint: Recursive DFS can overflow the stack on a 200 × 200 grid; a queue-based BFS is safer.

title: Shortest path in a maze
statement: A maze is a grid where . is open and # is a wall. Start at the top-left cell and reach the bottom-right cell, moving up, down, left or right. Print the fewest moves, or -1 if it cannot be done. Both corner cells are always open.
input: The first line has T. Each test case has a line with r and c, then r lines of c characters.
output: For each test case, print the fewest moves or -1.

title: Climbing stairs
statement: You climb a staircase of n steps, taking 1 or 2 steps at a time. Count the different ways to reach the top. For n = 3 there are 3 ways: 1+1+1, 1+2 and 2+1. The count grows fast, so print it modulo 1,000,000,007.
input: The first line has T. Each of the next T lines has n.
output: For each test case, print the number of ways modulo 1000000007.
hint: ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2). Precompute once up to 100000 if you like.

title: Fewest coins
statement: You have unlimited coins of some values. Find the fewest coins that add up to an amount exactly, or -1 if it cannot be made. With coins 1 5 6 9 and amount 11, the answer is 2 (5 + 6). Choosing the biggest coin first does not always work.
input: The first line has T. Each test case has a line with the number of coin values m and the amount, then a line with the m coin values.
output: For each test case, print the fewest coins or -1.

title: Anagrams
statement: Two words are anagrams if one is a rearrangement of the other's letters, like listen and silent. Count letters with an array of 26 or a hash map.
input: The first line has T. Each of the next T lines has two lowercase words.
output: For each pair, print YES if they are anagrams and NO otherwise.

title: Next greater element
statement: For every element, find the first element to its right that is strictly greater, or -1 if there is none. For 4 5 2 25 the answer is 5 25 25 -1. A monotonic stack does it in O(n).
input: The first line has T. Each test case has a line with n, then a line with n numbers.
output: For each test case, print n numbers on one line, separated by spaces.
constraints: Aim for O(n) with a stack.

title: Majority element
statement: An array has a value that appears more than n / 2 times. Find it. Can you do it with O(1) extra memory? (Look up the Boyer–Moore voting idea.)
input: The first line has T. Each test case has a line with n, then a line with n numbers.
output: For each test case, print the majority value.
